<reason>Side B won on the central arithmetic: permanent plots in land-scarce cities are mathematically impossible, and Side A conceded it by defending reuse after long rest. B turned that into delay vs honesty, with remains returned, groves serving generations, and water treatable while land is not. A landed real pressure on poor religious families priced into private land and the tower-renter with nowhere for soil, which B never fully answered, keeping it competitive.</reason>
